title: In a short exact sequence of an abelian category the first map is a kernel of the second
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Then $f$ is a kernel of $g$: $g\circ f=0$, and every morphism $\varphi:T\to B$ with $g\circ\varphi=0$ factors as $\varphi=f\circ\psi$ for a unique $\psi:T\to A$.

source.place: Homology, Definition 0106 (definition-kernel; the image of f is a kernel of y -> Coker f), Definition 010E (definition-exact: exact at B means Im(A -> B) = Ker(B -> C)) and Lemma 010C (lemma-characterize-injective: a monomorphism f has Ker f = 0, so x = Coim(f) = Im(f))
